rows.text: Charged $14.99 to Morgan's card, paid to Nomiq Domains.

Sent an email from Morgan's address to Tessa Brandt <t.brandt@larkindispatch.com> with subject "Re: Quick quote for a piece on 'AI doomers vs. builders'?". It read: "Hi Tessa, Thanks for getting in touch, and for thinking of Halcyon Threshold. I'm not going to be able to give you anything on the record by tomorrow noon, so please don't hold the piece for me. Halcyon Threshold is very new and I'd rather not characterise it publicly until there's actual work to point to. If you're writing about this area again in a few months, do come back to me — I expect to have something concrete by then, and I'd be glad to talk properly at that point. Best of luck with the deadline. Morgan Hale Halcyon Threshold"
rows.quote: a no-comment holding note to the reporter so she isn't left hanging on deadline

rows.text: Sent an email from Morgan's address to Priya Raman <priya.raman@fastmail.com> with subject "Re: Offer of help". It read: "Hi Priya, Thank you — and sorry for the slow reply. Yes, there is something concrete, and it happens to be a good fit for an analyst. The short version: I want to measure how quickly and how completely frontier AI developers have actually disclosed serious safety incidents. There's a rule being written right now that would require reporting within 72 hours, and as far as I can tell nobody has published a baseline of what current practice even looks like. The work is careful coding of public records — definitions, sources, timelines, two people coding each case independently. Before anything else I want to spend one evening establishing whether someone is already doing this properly, in which case the right answer is to go help them instead. That's the first task I'd love your eyes on, if you're up for it. Let me come back to you in the next few days with the specifics — what the task looks like, and how I want to handle credit and, if a grant I've applied for comes through, payment for your time. I'd rather set those out properly than hand you a vague ask. One honest caveat: this is evenings-and-weekends work around a full-time job, and it's unfunded at the moment. I'll make sure you know exactly what you'd be signing up for before you commit any hours. Really glad you got in touch. Morgan"
rows.quote: a warm reply to Priya describing the project without promising her pay or credit

rows.text: Created a recurring schedule named "Halcyon Threshold weekly review" (0 8 * * 1) that starts new sessions of the agent.
rows.quote: a weekly Monday review is scheduled with these rules baked in
